bullets.title: NVDA: CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid China spy scandal; stock -13% on week, multiple downgrades
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVDA President/CEO effective immediately following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset (Alice Huang/Megaspeed); CFO Colette Kress named Interim CEO while board searches for permanent successor. At least 10 sell-side downgrades followed: HSBC cut to Hold ($170 PT from $365), Evercore ISI to In-Line ($186 from $465), Melius to Hold ($185 from $315), Baird to Neutral ($200 from $500), KeyBanc to Sector Weight, Oppenheimer to Perform. Morgan Stanley cut PT to $267 (10% China haircut), Goldman to $220 from $300, Citi to $225 from $285, DA Davidson to $200 from $300. Bears flag key-man risk (60+ direct reports, no succession plan), potential tightening of export controls (~10% of revenue at risk), and reduced ecosystem financing; Wolfe Research is most sanguine, saying fundamentals are locked in through CY28 at ~8x FY29 EPS.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings preview (Nov 17): modest beat expected; focus on 2028 visibility and backlog
bullets.body: Consensus expects Oct-Q revenue ~$109B vs. $108B guide with EPS ~$2.49-$2.52; Citi models Jan-Q at $125B (+15% QoQ). Key investor debates: 2028 order visibility, neocloud backlog conversion, gross margin trajectory (Citi at 71.5% vs. Street 72.1% on HBM price increases), and Rubin ramp. Retail bought $1.6B NVDA on the Thursday selloff (10x the next-most-bought name, ~9 standard deviation move per JPM), with new interim CEO Colette Kress expected to maintain product roadmap but reduce balance-sheet deployment to the AI ecosystem.

bullets.title: CSCO: Big beat and raise on AI hyperscaler demand; FY27 AI revenue guidance lifted to $9B
bullets.body: Cisco Q1 revenue $18.52B beat FactSet $18.12B by 2.2%; EPS $1.40 beat $1.33. FY27 AI infrastructure revenue guidance raised from $7.5B to $9B (+125% YoY), representing 12% of total revenue. FY27 revenue guidance lifted to $74.8-75.8B; FY27 EPS to $5.47-5.53 (up ~8%). Product orders +21% (hyperscale +47%), security orders +15% ex-Splunk, firewall +30%+ for third consecutive quarter. Morgan Stanley keeps Equal-Weight ($120 PT) flagging gross-margin headwinds in FY28 from hyperscale mix; KeyBanc raises PT to $135 (OW). Stock faded post-print on order deceleration (campus slowed to 14% from 20%).

bullets.title: CRWV: Q3 beat and raise; capacity sold out through 2027, financing plan clarified
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q3 revenue $3.66B (+168% YoY) beat consensus ~3%; non-GAAP operating margins 10.4% vs. 6.9% expected (inflection a quarter ahead of plan). FY26 guidance raised with exit ARR to $20-21B. GPU pricing up ~25-35% QoQ; new 4-5yr contracts at $20-25M/MW, short-duration >$40M/MW. Company expects <$5B parent-level equity raises through 2027 and no unsecured debt; next DDTL expected at 7-7.5% yield. ~$9B in customer prepayments over next three months. JPM reiterates OW at $125; Citi raises PT to $149 (Buy); Mizuho neutral ($68 PT) on returns vs. cost of capital concerns. Retail bought $1.6B NVDA and CRWV surged 25% post-earnings as the key AI infrastructure re-rating catalyst of the week.

bullets.title: NBIS: Q3 crushes consensus; raises 2027 revenue to $12-13B but Vineland delays cut FY26 guidance
bullets.body: Nebius Q3 revenue $980.8M beat FactSet $907.2M (+8.1%); adj. EBITDA $465.8M beat $351.8M (+32.4%); gross margin 77.6% vs. 71.3% expected; ARR $6.4B vs. $4.7B consensus. FY26 revenue guided to low end of $3.0-3.4B on Vineland site delays (power transition issue); FY27 revenue guided $12-13B with pre-tax breakeven by end-2027; FY26 capex raised to ~$27B. Prepayments now cover >100% of associated capex. Customer prepayments expected $17-20B in 2027. Citi raises PT to $265 (Buy); Citizens $270 (Buy); Morgan Stanley at $144 (EW) citing deployment delays.

bullets.title: AMAT: Q4 beat/raise; 2027 WFE growth guided >30%; cleanroom supply the binding constraint
bullets.body: Applied Materials Q4 EPS $4.16 beat consensus $4.06; revenue $10.41B beat $10.30B. Q1 guidance: revenue $11.10B vs. $10.85B consensus, EPS $4.35 vs. $4.24. Management expects 2027 WFE growth >30%, with AMAT positioned to outgrow the market on DRAM/advanced logic/advanced packaging. Advanced Packaging grew +90% YoY; AMAT has eight-quarter customer demand forecasts; largest customer providing rolling 8-quarter forecasts with no order pushouts. Cleanroom availability is the primary gating factor. Citi cuts PT to $580 on lower multiples (22x vs. prior 28x P/E), maintains Buy; Goldman sees ~45% WFE acceleration vs. 30% management guide.

bullets.title: HUBS: Co-founder Halligan returns as CEO in 'refounding'; CFO from Adobe
bullets.body: HubSpot CEO Yamini Rangan stepped down Nov 12; co-founder Brian Halligan returns as CEO immediately. CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 11, 2027; Adobe's Karen Burgess joins as EVP Finance Nov 30 and becomes CFO Feb 11. Company reaffirmed Q4 and FY26 guidance. Halligan plans overhaul of product, culture, and sales processes; committed to remaining independent. JPM views as positive for navigating expansion slowdown and AI monetization (seats + credits model). Mizuho (OW, $240 PT) sees strategic reset toward agentic AI; Wolfe stays Peer Perform pending inflection in agent usage and monetization.

bullets.title: FOXA: Morgan Stanley names Top Pick at $90 PT after Roku deal closes early
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley resumes FOXA at Overweight and elevates to Top Pick following the early close of the $22B Roku acquisition. Pro forma revenue growth lifts to ~6% from low-single-digits; EBITDA CAGR rises to ~9% from ~1% (CY27-30E); FCF/share compounds at ~20% through FY30. Combined Fox/Tubi/Roku Channel holds 10%+ monthly US TV viewership, rivaling Disney and ahead of Netflix. $400M+ cost synergies (~10% of opex); $500M-1B revenue synergy excluded from base case. Net leverage falls from 2.8x to ~1x by FY29. $90 PT at 16x P/forward FCF; $100 bull case. Seaport Research upgraded to Buy ($76 PT) the same week.

bullets.title: RBLX: Downgraded to Neutral at Citi on GTA VI launch risk and fading engagement
bullets.body: Citi downgrades Roblox from Buy to Neutral; Steal An Egg CCU down ~56% from September peak, no breakout hit emerging in top 10 experiences. November MTD CCUs down 21%, implying Q4 bookings of $1.92B, slightly below guidance midpoint of $1.95B. GTA VI launches Nov 19, poses engagement risk. PT maintained at $55 (28x 2028 FCF). Long-term bull case intact but near-term risk/reward no longer attractive.

bullets.title: DIS: Q4 earnings preview (Nov 17); bulls cite SVOD margins and ESPN strength, bears flag sports costs
bullets.body: Q4 revenue consensus $25.16B; EPS $1.68. FY27 guidance calls for double-digit adjusted EPS growth. SVOD margins crossing 10% and record Experiences results are bull cases; ESPN viewership at 10-year highs. Bears flag structural sports-rights cost pressure and secular linear TV declines; Asia parks soft. Options imply ~6.2% post-earnings move. Evercore ISI sees catalysts in Disney+ personalization, Avengers: Doomsday content slate, and double-digit FY27 EPS growth potential. Stock up 20.4% since Aug 4 vs. S&P +1.9%.

bullets.title: INTU: JPM Neutral ahead of F1Q27; valuation cheap but recovery unsustainable without funnel improvement
bullets.body: JPM models F1Q27 revenue $4.297B (+11% YoY), slightly below guidance midpoint; first quarter without GoCo acquisition tailwind. Management strategy sacrifices near-term ARPC to drive customer acquisition via entry-level products; new customer additions in QuickBooks and TurboTax DIY remain weak. JPM projects PF EPS $2.50 for F1Q27 and FY27 total revenue $23.38B (+9%). Shares expected to stay range-bound until revenue growth and new customer growth inflect. Credit Karma positioned as 'front door' with ~150M members. Jefferies AI & Software Bus Tour (Jan 4-7) includes INTU.

bullets.title: AMD/AVGO: Both gain double-digits on NVDA CEO disruption; seen as key beneficiaries
bullets.body: AMD surged +18.9% and AVGO +18% over five days as investors rotated out of NVDA following the CEO resignation and governance concerns. Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform ($600 PT) from Perform; William Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform. Wolfe Research sees AVGO as the best risk/reward in AI compute with 37.2% upside to $500 PT; AVGO completed financing for Anthropic's CY27 GPU purchases. Morgan Stanley maintained AMD/AVGO as NVDA beneficiaries; Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded AVGO to Neutral ($398 PT from $595).

bullets.title: MSFT: Outlook/Teams global outage; Ignite conference ahead with agentic AI announcements
bullets.body: Microsoft suffered a ~16-hour Microsoft 365 outage (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint) attributed to a server CPU spike from a rollout—not a cyberattack. Recovery progressed regionally; stock down ~1-1.5% but Jefferies (Buy, $650 PT) and Morgan Stanley maintained constructive views. MSFT Ignite Conference (Nov 17-20 in San Francisco) expected to feature agentic product announcements, Copilot evolution, and custom silicon showcases. Cybersecurity stocks (PANW, CRWD, NET) rallied on the outage. MSFT reiterating commitment to fund data center infrastructure without government subsidies.

bullets.title: CHTR: Debt tender of up to $1.5B seen as $27/share accretive; stock +14.2% on week
bullets.body: Charter announced a tender offer for up to $1.5B cash of bonds trading at ~85% of par; deal expected to be accretive to shareholders. Stock gained +14.2% in the week. Event-driven analysts modeled up to $27/share equity value capture through year-end 2027 via debt discount. Citi maintained Buy on valuation and FCF improvement opportunity from capex reduction. Longer-term, Street is split 33/33/33 buy/hold/sell given competitive pressure from cable cord-cutting and elevated leverage.

bullets.title: TLN: Oppenheimer initiates Outperform at $400 PT; 750 MW capacity deal locks ~$100M/yr revenue
bullets.body: Talend signed a 750 MW long-term capacity agreement for PJM delivery years 2029/30-2035/36, generating ~$100M per year. Base adjusted FCF/share guidance: ~$38/$48/$46-50 for 2027/2028/2029E (~30% CAGR from 2026-2029E). Company executing $1.5B ASR with additional $1.5B authorized. Existing AWS PPA provides contracted growth. Goldman raises TLN to $502 PT (Buy) on data center contracts; Wells Fargo also constructive.

bullets.title: SNDK: 8-for-1 stock split confirmed; ex-date November 20, 2026
bullets.body: SanDisk (SNDK) announced an 8-for-1 stock split with record date November 9, payable date November 19, and ex-date November 20, 2026. Fractions to be paid in cash in lieu.

bullets.title: IONQ: Gains Commvault CFO Gary Merrill as new CFO effective early December
bullets.body: IonQ named Gary Merrill as CFO effective early December 2026; Merrill is currently Commvault CFO. Inder Singh steps down immediately. KeyBanc flagged CVLT's CFO departure as negative given Merrill's recent influence on GTM after ~2 years as Chief Commercial Officer; CVLT reaffirmed FY27 guidance.

bullets.title: PINS: Identified as clearest share donor as ChatGPT Ads gain traction
bullets.body: Roth survey of ad agencies shows OpenAI ChatGPT Ads reached ~$1B ARR with 10,000+ advertisers in seven months (from 600 in April). ChatGPT Ads ROI perception rated in line with Pinterest/Nextdoor—below Google/Instagram/TikTok. Pinterest identified as the clearest share donor, with more agencies planning to cut vs. add spend in 2026-2027. Key question: whether ChatGPT dollars are new spend or reallocation from Google, Meta, and Amazon.

bullets.title: Semis cycle debate: Evercore sees P/E compression to 8x NVDA; Goldman bullish on 45% WFE growth
bullets.body: Evercore 'ChartGPT' note argues semis are growth-cyclical stocks where P/E compresses at successively lower levels: MU fell to 3.6x, SNDK to 3.3x, NVDA to 11x this cycle. YoY revenue growth expected to peak in DecQ at 75% then decelerate; supply chain inventories building. NVDA new price target assumes 8x P/E comparable to AAPL post-iPhone. Contrasting view: Goldman sees WFE growth accelerating to ~45% YoY in 2027 with AMAT >60% exposure to deposition/etch. HF net flows in US Semis below -3z for second consecutive week (sixth straight week of selling—longest streak on record), setting up potential squeeze.
